name: AbleTo
one_liner: 8-week CBT-based therapy and coaching by phone or video, offered as a benefit through some US health plans and employers.
best_for: Adults whose health plan or employer includes AbleTo as a covered benefit
People with mild to moderate depression, anxiety or stress who want a short, structured CBT program
People living with a medical condition such as heart disease or diabetes who also feel low or anxious
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People whose health plan does not include AbleTo
People who need medication or a psychiatric prescriber
People who want open-ended, long-term therapy
short_description: AbleTo runs 8-week CBT programs with a licensed therapist and a coach by phone or video, available through some health plans at little or no cost.
long_description: AbleTo is a US virtual behavioral health service sold to health plans and employers rather than directly to the public; press reported in 2020 that UnitedHealth Group's Optum was buying it for about $470 million. Its programs run for 8 weeks and use cognitive behavioral therapy, delivered by phone or secure video with a licensed therapist, with a behavioral coach alongside. AbleTo says it is a covered benefit for more than 26 million people and that most participants pay nothing, though copays and deductibles depend on your plan; late rescheduling can incur a $45 fee. The published research is uncontrolled: a 2018 before-after study of 1,482 program graduates found large drops in depression scores, and a 2021 retrospective study of its self-guided AbleTo Digital+ app reported symptom improvement among people who completed at least four modules.

pricing.starting_price: Free or copay through your health plan or employer; no self-pay option published
pricing.notes: AbleTo says it is a fully covered benefit with no cost-share for most participants; copays and deductibles depend on your plan. Rescheduling with less than 24 hours' notice may carry a $45 fee.

privacy.notes: AbleTo's HIPAA notice of privacy practices covers your treatment records and lets you request amendments, but it does not address sale of data, ad sharing or deletion, and no website privacy policy could be found.

faqs.q: Is AbleTo free or covered by insurance?
faqs.a: AbleTo is typically offered at no cost to employees through employer health benefits or insurance plans. You cannot sign up directly—access comes through your employer or health plan. Check with your HR department or insurance provider to see if AbleTo is included in your benefits.

AbleTo provides structured 8-week programs combining weekly 30-minute video sessions with a licensed therapist plus weekly check-in calls with a behavioral coach. Programs use evidence-based CBT techniques for anxiety, depression, stress, chronic pain, and substance use. After the initial program, maintenance sessions may be available.

faqs.q: Is AbleTo effective for anxiety and depression?
faqs.a: Clinical studies show AbleTo members experience 50% average improvement in depression and anxiety symptoms. The structured program format with both therapy and coaching support leads to high completion rates. AbleTo is designed for mild to moderate symptoms—those with severe conditions may need more intensive care.

faqs.q: How is AbleTo different from BetterHelp or Talkspace?
faqs.a: Unlike BetterHelp and Talkspace which are direct-to-consumer, AbleTo is accessed through employer benefits at no cost. AbleTo uses structured 8-week programs rather than ongoing unlimited therapy. It also includes coaching support alongside therapy. If your employer offers AbleTo, it's typically the most cost-effective option.

Coping with depression or anxiety alongside a medical condition

patient_summary: You can use AbleTo only if your health plan or employer covers it; you check your coverage on its site or AbleTo may contact you. You then meet a licensed therapist by phone or video for an 8-week CBT program, with a coach for support between sessions. Most participants pay nothing, but your plan's copay or deductible may apply.

availability.note: Only through participating health plans and employers in the US; not sold directly to individuals.
